ai.definition: A recursive intelligence layer is an AI infrastructure component that continuously analyzes, upgrades, expands, and corrects the entire system. It operates as a meta-cognitive agent dedicated to enhancing the overall intelligence of the platform.
ai.howItWorks: The recursive intelligence layer proactively scans for missing content, inconsistencies, thin sections, and opportunities for expansion. It then makes necessary corrections and updates to improve the system's performance and efficiency.
ai.problemSolved: Continuous improvement and maintenance of AI systems without human intervention.
ai.manufacturing: N/A (the technology is conceptual at this stage)
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves developing algorithms for continuous analysis, updating, and expansion. It requires a robust framework to support the recursive nature of self-improvement.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Early conceptual stage with potential for significant future development and commercialization
ai.regulation: No specific regulations currently exist, but adherence to general data protection and privacy laws will be necessary.
ai.profitability: Uncertain at this stage; potential for significant long-term benefits if successfully implemented
ai.futureDevelopment: Further refinement of algorithms, integration with other AI systems, and expansion into various applications.

glossary.def: An AI system capable of self-reflection and improvement
A component that continuously analyzes, upgrades, expands, and corrects the entire platform
